```{r}
# The preregistered (Stage 1) analyses were frequentist: lme4 models, H1 judged
# by the 90% CI against the SESOI, H2 by joint Wald tests. This chunk fits
# them in one place for Appendix D (@tbl-frequentist-registered): on the
# analytic sample, under two preregistered specifications (all five platforms
# for H1, Deviation D4; primary-genre attribution for H2, D1), and on the
# earlier sample that D7 corrects (Open Play v1.2.1, 1,838 participants). It
# sits here, after h2-wald, because it reuses that chunk's objects and
# Appendix A (D7) quotes its results before Appendix D is reached.
# lme4 only; no brms fit is loaded.

# Preregistered decision grid for H1 (Stage 1 Design Table, pre-registration
# PDF p. 31), applied to the 90% CI [lb, ub]. The Design Table lists
# "LB > [-.06]" for a practically significant positive association, which we
# read as LB > .06 (the counterpart of UB < -.06). Its "absence of a
# practically significant association" (LB > -.06 and UB < .06) overlaps the
# "not practically significant" positive and negative classes; the more
# specific class applies to intervals that exclude zero, so the absence class
# is used for intervals inside the bounds that cover zero. The order of the
# case_when() conditions implements this.
reg_sesoi <- 0.06
reg_h1_verdict <- function(lb, ub, sesoi = reg_sesoi) {
  dplyr::case_when(
    lb > sesoi                   ~ "Practically significant positive association",
    ub < -sesoi                  ~ "Practically significant negative association",
    lb > 0 & ub > sesoi          ~ "Positive association, may be practically significant",
    ub < 0 & lb < -sesoi         ~ "Negative association, may be practically significant",
    lb > 0 & ub < sesoi          ~ "Positive association, not practically significant",
    ub < 0 & lb > -sesoi         ~ "Negative association, not practically significant",
    lb > -sesoi & ub < sesoi     ~ "No practically significant association",
    TRUE                         ~ "Inconclusive"
  )
}
# The three classes in which an H1 coefficient is not practically significant
# (together: the 90% CI lies strictly inside the SESOI bounds).
reg_h1_nps <- c("No practically significant association",
                "Negative association, not practically significant",
                "Positive association, not practically significant")
# Unit check of the grid on constructed intervals (one per class).
stopifnot(identical(
  reg_h1_verdict(c(0.07, -0.09, 0.01, -0.08, 0.01, -0.03, -0.02, -0.07),
                 c(0.09, -0.07, 0.08, -0.01, 0.03, -0.01, 0.02, 0.01)),
  c("Practically significant positive association",
    "Practically significant negative association",
    "Positive association, may be practically significant",
    "Negative association, may be practically significant",
    "Positive association, not practically significant",
    "Negative association, not practically significant",
    "No practically significant association",
    "Inconclusive")))
# Preregistered decision rule for H2: p < .05 on the joint Wald test means at
# least two genres differ.
reg_h2_verdict <- function(p) {
  ifelse(p < 0.05, "Equality rejected (supported)",
         "Equality not rejected (not supported)")
}

# Analysis frame exactly as chunk model-data builds analysis_data (guarded
# below), so every specification shares one code path: genre hours pivoted
# wide and zero-filled, person-mean centring over all of a participant's
# survey waves.
build_analysis_frame <- function(survey, total_playtime, genre_wave_long) {
  genre_hours_wide <- genre_wave_long |>
    mutate(col = {
      clean <- gsub("[^a-z0-9]+", "_", tolower(genre))
      clean <- gsub("^_+|_+$", "", clean)
      clean <- gsub("__+", "_", clean)
      paste0("gh_", clean)
    }) |>
    select(pid, wave, col, hours_per_day) |>
    pivot_wider(names_from = col, values_from = hours_per_day, values_fill = 0)
  gh_vars <- sort(setdiff(names(genre_hours_wide), c("pid", "wave")))
  survey |>
    select(pid, wave, wemwbs) |>
    left_join(
      total_playtime |> select(pid, wave, total_hours_per_day),
      by = c("pid", "wave")
    ) |>
    left_join(genre_hours_wide, by = c("pid", "wave")) |>
    mutate(
      total_hours_per_day = replace_na(total_hours_per_day, 0),
      across(all_of(gh_vars), ~ replace_na(.x, 0))
    ) |>
    group_by(pid) |>
    mutate(
      total_within  = total_hours_per_day -
                        mean(total_hours_per_day, na.rm = TRUE),
      total_between = mean(total_hours_per_day, na.rm = TRUE),
      across(
        all_of(gh_vars),
        list(
          within  = ~ .x - mean(.x, na.rm = TRUE),
          between = ~ mean(.x, na.rm = TRUE)
        ),
        .names = "{.col}_{.fn}"
      )
    ) |>
    ungroup()
}
stopifnot(identical(build_analysis_frame(survey, total_playtime, genre_wave_long),
                    analysis_data))

# H1 as preregistered: random intercept and correlated random slope for
# within-person playtime; Wald 90% CIs.
fit_h1_reg <- function(d, x = "total") {
  f <- as.formula(sprintf("wemwbs ~ %1$s_within + %1$s_between + (1 + %1$s_within | pid)", x))
  fit <- lmer(f, data = d |> filter(!is.na(wemwbs)),
              control = lmerControl(optimizer = "bobyqa"))
  terms <- paste0(x, c("_within", "_between"))
  ci <- confint(fit, parm = terms, level = 0.90, method = "Wald")
  tibble(term = c("within", "between"), estimate = unname(lme4::fixef(fit)[terms]),
         lo = unname(ci[terms, 1]), hi = unname(ci[terms, 2]),
         n_pid = unname(lme4::ngrps(fit)["pid"]), n_obs = nobs(fit),
         singular = isSingular(fit)) |>
    mutate(verdict = reg_h1_verdict(lo, hi))
}

# H2 as tested in chunk h2-wald (ML, random intercept, 13 equality
# constraints per dimension); the SD of the 14 coefficients is descriptive.
fit_h2_reg <- function(d) {
  gw <- sort(grep("^gh_.*_within$", names(d), value = TRUE))
  gb <- sort(grep("^gh_.*_between$", names(d), value = TRUE))
  f <- paste("wemwbs ~", paste(c(gw, gb), collapse = " + "), "+ (1 | pid)")
  fit <- suppressWarnings(suppressMessages(
    lmer(as.formula(f), data = d |> filter(!is.na(wemwbs)), REML = FALSE,
         control = lmerControl(optimizer = "bobyqa", calc.derivs = FALSE))
  ))
  wa <- car::linearHypothesis(fit, paste0(gw[1], " = ", gw[-1]))
  wb <- car::linearHypothesis(fit, paste0(gb[1], " = ", gb[-1]))
  out <- tibble(term = c("within", "between"),
                chisq = c(wa$Chisq[2], wb$Chisq[2]), df = c(wa$Df[2], wb$Df[2]),
                p = c(wa$`Pr(>Chisq)`[2], wb$`Pr(>Chisq)`[2]),
                sd_coef = c(sd(lme4::fixef(fit)[gw]), sd(lme4::fixef(fit)[gb])),
                n_pid = unname(lme4::ngrps(fit)["pid"]), n_obs = nobs(fit)) |>
    mutate(verdict = reg_h2_verdict(p))
  attr(out, "fit") <- fit
  out
}

# --- H1, analytic sample, console/PC total (preregistered model) --------------
reg_h1_main <- fit_h1_reg(analysis_data)

# --- H1, all five platforms (preregistered exposure, D4) -----------------------
# Mobile minutes are joined to the survey frame directly, so waves with
# mobile play but no console/PC play keep their mobile minutes.
analysis_data_allplat <- analysis_data |>
  select(pid, wave, wemwbs, total_hours_per_day) |>
  left_join(mobile, by = c("pid", "wave")) |>
  mutate(mobile_hours_per_day = replace_na(mobile_hours_per_day, 0),
         allplat = total_hours_per_day + mobile_hours_per_day) |>
  group_by(pid) |>
  mutate(allplat_within  = allplat - mean(allplat, na.rm = TRUE),
         allplat_between = mean(allplat, na.rm = TRUE)) |>
  ungroup()
reg_h1_allplat <- fit_h1_reg(analysis_data_allplat, x = "allplat")
allplat_obs <- analysis_data_allplat |> filter(!is.na(wemwbs))
reg_n_mobile_pids  <- n_distinct(allplat_obs$pid[allplat_obs$mobile_hours_per_day > 0])
reg_pct_mobile_pw  <- 100 * mean(allplat_obs$mobile_hours_per_day > 0)
reg_pct_mobile_time <- 100 * sum(allplat_obs$mobile_hours_per_day) /
  sum(allplat_obs$allplat)

# --- H2, analytic sample, full attribution: reuse chunk h2-wald -------------
reg_h2_main <- tibble(
  term = c("within", "between"),
  chisq = c(h2_cc_wald_a$Chisq[2], h2_cc_wald_b$Chisq[2]),
  df = c(h2_cc_wald_a$Df[2], h2_cc_wald_b$Df[2]),
  p = c(h2_cc_wald_a$`Pr(>Chisq)`[2], h2_cc_wald_b$`Pr(>Chisq)`[2]),
  sd_coef = c(sd_within_cc, sd_between_cc),
  n_pid = unname(lme4::ngrps(h2_cc_fit)["pid"]), n_obs = nobs(h2_cc_fit)
) |>
  mutate(verdict = reg_h2_verdict(p))
# fit_h2_reg() is the h2-wald code path: it reproduces those tests exactly.
reg_h2_check <- fit_h2_reg(analysis_data)
stopifnot(isTRUE(all.equal(reg_h2_check$p, reg_h2_main$p)),
          isTRUE(all.equal(reg_h2_check$sd_coef, reg_h2_main$sd_coef)))
rm(reg_h2_check)

# --- H2, primary-genre attribution (preregistered rule, D1) --------------------
# R/prep_primary_genre.R: each game's full playtime goes to its first IGDB
# genre that survives the study taxonomy; sample, waves and taxonomy as above.
genre_wave_long_primary <- read_csv(
  here("data/processed/genre_wave_long_primary.csv"), show_col_types = FALSE)
analysis_data_primary <- build_analysis_frame(survey, total_playtime,
                                              genre_wave_long_primary)
stopifnot(
  identical(sort(grep("^gh_.*_within$", names(analysis_data_primary), value = TRUE)),
            sort(gh_within)),
  identical(analysis_data_primary$total_within, analysis_data$total_within)
)
reg_h2_primary <- fit_h2_reg(analysis_data_primary)

# --- Earlier sample of D7 (v1.2.1: anyone with a valid SWEMWBS) -------------
# Same code path: the v1.2.1 survey file (with its own baseline days) and
# the v1.2.1 processed telemetry kept in data/processed_v121/.
pids_v121 <- analytic_pids("data/clean_v121", require_qualified = FALSE)
survey_v121 <- load_survey_data(pids_v121, clean_dir = "data/clean_v121",
                                baseline_days = NULL)
analysis_data_v121 <- build_analysis_frame(
  survey_v121,
  read_csv(here("data/processed_v121/total_playtime.csv"), show_col_types = FALSE),
  read_csv(here("data/processed_v121/genre_wave_long.csv"), show_col_types = FALSE)
)
# The earlier sample is the analytic sample plus the participants D7 removes,
# and its frame is row-identical to analysis_data for the retained ones.
stopifnot(
  isTRUE(all.equal(
    as.data.frame(arrange(filter(analysis_data_v121, pid %in% analysis_pids), pid, wave)),
    as.data.frame(arrange(analysis_data, pid, wave)), check.attributes = FALSE)),
  length(pids_v121) == n_model + n_revoked_in_sample + n_no_intake_v121,
  all(analysis_pids %in% pids_v121),
  identical(sort(grep("^gh_.*_within$", names(analysis_data_v121), value = TRUE)),
            sort(gh_within))
)
reg_h1_v121 <- fit_h1_reg(analysis_data_v121)
reg_h2_v121 <- fit_h2_reg(analysis_data_v121)

# --- Preregistered random-slope structure for H2 (chunk h2-wald) ---------------
# The preregistered uncorrelated per-participant slopes for the 14 within-person
# genre terms, fitted by ML on each H2 frame: the analytic sample (h2-wald),
# primary attribution and the earlier sample (about 5 s each). Appendix D
# fits every H2 model with a random intercept because all three are singular.
fit_h2_slopes_reg <- function(d) {
  gw <- sort(grep("^gh_.*_within$", names(d), value = TRUE))
  gb <- sort(grep("^gh_.*_between$", names(d), value = TRUE))
  f <- paste("wemwbs ~", paste(c(gw, gb), collapse = " + "),
             "+ (1 +", paste(gw, collapse = " + "), "|| pid)")
  fit <- suppressMessages(lmer(
    as.formula(f), data = d |> filter(!is.na(wemwbs)), REML = FALSE,
    control = lmerControl(optimizer = "bobyqa", optCtrl = list(maxfun = 1e5))
  ))
  vc <- as.data.frame(VarCorr(fit))
  list(singular = isSingular(fit), n_zero = sum(vc$sdcor[vc$var1 %in% gw] < 1e-4))
}
reg_slopes_singular <- isSingular(h2_cc_slopes)
reg_slopes_n_zero   <- h2_cc_slopes_n_zero
reg_slopes_primary  <- fit_h2_slopes_reg(analysis_data_primary)
reg_slopes_v121     <- fit_h2_slopes_reg(analysis_data_v121)

# --- Primary attribution: why the between-person SD is large ----------------
# Under primary attribution a multi-genre game counts for one genre only, so
# genres that are rarely listed first rest on few players. Players per genre
# = participants with any play of that genre in an observed person-wave.
reg_primary_fit <- attr(reg_h2_primary, "fit")
reg_primary_obs <- analysis_data_primary |> filter(!is.na(wemwbs))
reg_full_obs    <- analysis_data |> filter(!is.na(wemwbs))
reg_genre_players <- tibble(var = sort(gh_vars)) |>
  mutate(
    n_primary = vapply(var, \(v) n_distinct(reg_primary_obs$pid[reg_primary_obs[[v]] > 0]), integer(1)),
    n_full    = vapply(var, \(v) n_distinct(reg_full_obs$pid[reg_full_obs[[v]] > 0]), integer(1)),
    b_between  = unname(lme4::fixef(reg_primary_fit)[paste0(var, "_between")]),
    se_between = unname(sqrt(diag(as.matrix(vcov(reg_primary_fit))))[
      match(paste0(var, "_between"), names(lme4::fixef(reg_primary_fit)))])
  )
reg_rare <- reg_genre_players |> slice_min(n_primary, n = 1, with_ties = FALSE)
reg_sd_between_primary_wo_rare <- sd(reg_genre_players$b_between[reg_genre_players$var != reg_rare$var])
reg_rare_label <- prettify_genre(sub("^gh_", "", reg_rare$var))  # mm-formula-setup

# --- Guards for the fixed prose (Appendix D, Results, Appendix A) -----------
reg_h1_all <- bind_rows(reg_h1_main, reg_h1_allplat, reg_h1_v121)
stopifnot(
  # Preregistered H1 grid on the analytic sample (Results, Appendix D, D7): no
  # practically significant association within persons; a negative
  # association that is not practically significant between persons (90% CI
  # below zero and above -0.06)
  identical(reg_h1_main$verdict, c("No practically significant association",
                                   "Negative association, not practically significant")),
  reg_h1_main$hi[2] < 0, reg_h1_main$lo[2] > -reg_sesoi,
  # no H1 row in any specification is, or may be, practically significant
  # (Results H1 intro, Robustness, Methods Missing Data, Discussion)
  all(reg_h1_all$verdict %in% reg_h1_nps),
  # H2 on the analytic sample: H2a rejected, H2b not (as in h2-wald)
  reg_h2_main$p[1] < 0.05, reg_h2_main$p[2] >= 0.05,
  # earlier sample: same H1 verdicts and same Wald decisions (D7)
  identical(reg_h1_v121$verdict, reg_h1_main$verdict),
  identical(reg_h2_v121$verdict, reg_h2_main$verdict),
  # D7 prose: within-person slope unchanged, between-person slope slightly
  # closer to zero on the corrected sample
  abs(reg_h1_main$estimate[1] - reg_h1_v121$estimate[1]) < 0.001,
  abs(reg_h1_main$estimate[2]) < abs(reg_h1_v121$estimate[2]),
  abs(reg_h1_main$estimate[2] - reg_h1_v121$estimate[2]) < 0.005,
  # all-platform H1 (Appendix D, D4, Discussion): same within-person
  # verdict; the between-person interval includes zero, so that coefficient
  # shows no practically significant association; mobile a small share
  reg_h1_allplat$verdict[1] == reg_h1_main$verdict[1],
  reg_h1_allplat$verdict[2] == "No practically significant association",
  reg_h1_allplat$lo[2] < 0, reg_h1_allplat$hi[2] > 0,
  reg_pct_mobile_time < 5,
  # primary attribution: neither joint test rejects equality
  all(reg_h2_primary$p >= 0.05),
  # the primary between-person SD is driven by the least-played genre: it
  # has the largest between-person coefficient, a standard error above 1,
  # and the SD of the other 13 is a small fraction of the SD of all 14
  reg_genre_players$var[which.max(abs(reg_genre_players$b_between))] == reg_rare$var,
  reg_rare$se_between > 1,
  reg_sd_between_primary_wo_rare < reg_h2_primary$sd_coef[2] / 5,
  reg_rare$n_primary < reg_rare$n_full,
  # preregistered random-slope structure singular in all three H2 frames
  # (Appendix D prose and table note), most slope SDs at zero
  reg_slopes_singular, reg_slopes_n_zero > length(gh_within) / 2,
  reg_slopes_primary$singular, reg_slopes_primary$n_zero > length(gh_within) / 2,
  reg_slopes_v121$singular, reg_slopes_v121$n_zero > length(gh_within) / 2
)

f3  <- function(x) sprintf("%.3f", x)
f4  <- function(x) sprintf("%.4f", x)
fci <- function(lo, hi) sprintf("[%.4f, %.4f]", lo, hi)
fn  <- function(x) formatC(x, format = "d", big.mark = ",")
txt_reg_n_v121_pid <- fn(reg_h1_v121$n_pid[1])

txt_reg_b_v121_ci <- fci(reg_h1_v121$lo[2], reg_h1_v121$hi[2])
txt_reg_b_allplat <- f4(reg_h1_allplat$estimate[2])
txt_reg_b_allplat_ci <- fci(reg_h1_allplat$lo[2], reg_h1_allplat$hi[2])
txt_reg_p_main_a <- f3(reg_h2_main$p[1])
txt_reg_p_main_b <- f3(reg_h2_main$p[2])
txt_reg_p_v121_a <- f3(reg_h2_v121$p[1])
txt_reg_p_v121_b <- f3(reg_h2_v121$p[2])
txt_reg_chisq_primary_a <- sprintf("%.1f", reg_h2_primary$chisq[1])
txt_reg_chisq_primary_b <- sprintf("%.1f", reg_h2_primary$chisq[2])
txt_reg_df_primary <- reg_h2_primary$df[1]
txt_reg_p_primary_a <- f3(reg_h2_primary$p[1])
txt_reg_p_primary_b <- f3(reg_h2_primary$p[2])
txt_reg_sd_primary_w <- f3(reg_h2_primary$sd_coef[1])
txt_reg_sd_primary_b <- f3(reg_h2_primary$sd_coef[2])
txt_reg_sd_main_w <- f3(reg_h2_main$sd_coef[1])
txt_reg_sd_primary_b_wo <- f3(reg_sd_between_primary_wo_rare)
txt_reg_rare_label <- reg_rare_label
txt_reg_rare_n_primary <- fn(unname(reg_rare$n_primary))
txt_reg_rare_n_full <- fn(unname(reg_rare$n_full))
txt_reg_rare_se <- sprintf("%.2f", reg_rare$se_between)
txt_reg_n_mobile_pids <- fn(reg_n_mobile_pids)
txt_reg_pct_mobile_pw <- sprintf("%.1f", reg_pct_mobile_pw)
txt_reg_pct_mobile_time <- sprintf("%.1f", reg_pct_mobile_time)
txt_reg_slopes_n_zero <- reg_slopes_n_zero
txt_reg_slopes_n_zero_primary <- reg_slopes_primary$n_zero
txt_reg_slopes_n_zero_v121 <- reg_slopes_v121$n_zero
```

```{r}
#| label: txt-genre-differences-h2-1
#| include: false

# Inline quantities for the paragraph(s) below, defined once here so the
# prose reads `r name` rather than a formatting call.
txt_wald_a_chisq <- sprintf("%.1f", h2_cc_wald_a$Chisq[2])
txt_wald_a_p <- sprintf("%.3f", h2_cc_wald_a$"Pr(>Chisq)"[2])
txt_wald_b_chisq <- sprintf("%.1f", h2_cc_wald_b$Chisq[2])
txt_wald_b_p <- sprintf("%.3f", h2_cc_wald_b$"Pr(>Chisq)"[2])
```

The preregistered inference for H2 is a joint Wald test of whether the 14 genre coefficients are equal. We fitted a frequentist version of M2 by maximum likelihood, with the same fixed effects and random intercept, and tested the equality of its coefficients. The null hypothesis sets the 13 differences between the first genre's coefficient and each of the others to zero, which holds only if all 14 coefficients are equal; rejecting it means that at least one difference is non-zero, and hence that at least two genres differ. Within persons, the test rejected equality (χ²(`r h2_cc_wald_a$Df[2]`) = `r txt_wald_a_chisq`, *p* = `r txt_wald_a_p`): at least two genres differed in how a change in their playtime related to a change in wellbeing. Between persons, the test did not reject equality (χ²(`r h2_cc_wald_b$Df[2]`) = `r txt_wald_b_chisq`, *p* = `r txt_wald_b_p`). Under the preregistered criteria, H2a was supported and H2b was not. Appendix D reports these tests together with the preregistered H1 equivalence tests, under two preregistered specifications and on the earlier sample that Deviation D7 corrects (@tbl-frequentist-registered); under the preregistered primary-genre attribution, the within-person test did not reject equality (*p* = `r txt_reg_p_primary_a`).

```{r}
#| label: h2-joint-test
#| include: false
#| eval: true

# H2 is answered by the preregistered joint Wald tests (chunk h2-wald). The
# spread of the genre effects is DESCRIBED here, without a verdict (Methods,
# SESOI): the preregistration fixed no threshold for differences between genres.
# Reference values only (quoted in the Methods and the figure caption):
#   het_thr  = sesoi / 1.96            -> 95% of genre effects within the SESOI
#                                         of the average genre effect;
#   pair_thr = sesoi / (1.96 sqrt(2))  -> 95% of genre pairs within the SESOI
#                                         of each other.
# Whether genre effects also lie inside the ROPE depends on the centre as
# well (the *_rope_out shares below and in h2-hier-tau).
sesoi    <- 0.06
het_thr  <- sesoi / qnorm(0.975)
pair_thr <- sesoi / (qnorm(0.975) * sqrt(2))
# The Methods and the fig-h2-heterogeneity caption type these as 0.031, 0.022.
stopifnot(round(het_thr, 3) == 0.031, round(pair_thr, 3) == 0.022)
# Descriptors of a spread s, evaluated at each posterior draw:
#   het_share()  share of genres whose effect lies more than the SESOI from
#                the average genre effect under Normal(average, s);
#   pair_share() share of genre pairs whose effects differ by more than the
#                SESOI (a difference of two draws has SD sqrt(2) * s).
het_share  <- function(s) 2 * (1 - pnorm(sesoi, 0, s))
pair_share <- function(s) 2 * (1 - pnorm(sesoi / (sqrt(2) * s)))
# Expected number of the 14 genres beyond the SESOI, formatted for the prose
# (two decimals below one genre, one decimal otherwise).
fmt_n14 <- function(p) {
  n <- 14 * p
  if (n < 1) sprintf("%.2f", n) else sprintf("%.1f", n)
}

h2_draws <- posterior::as_draws_df(h2_model)

# brms names fixed effects as b_{varname}
within_cols <- paste0("b_", gh_within)
within_mat  <- as.matrix(h2_draws[, within_cols, drop = FALSE])

genre_effect_sd   <- apply(within_mat, 1, sd)
genre_sd_mean     <- mean(genre_effect_sd)
genre_sd_ci       <- quantile(genre_effect_sd, probs = c(0.025, 0.975))
genre_share       <- het_share(genre_effect_sd)
genre_share_mean  <- mean(genre_share)
genre_share_ci    <- quantile(genre_share, probs = c(0.025, 0.975))
genre_pair        <- pair_share(genre_effect_sd)
genre_pair_mean   <- mean(genre_pair)
genre_pair_ci     <- quantile(genre_pair, probs = c(0.025, 0.975))

# Same for between-person effects
between_cols      <- paste0("b_", gh_between)
between_mat       <- as.matrix(h2_draws[, between_cols, drop = FALSE])
genre_between_sd  <- apply(between_mat, 1, sd)
genre_bsd_mean    <- mean(genre_between_sd)
genre_bsd_ci      <- quantile(genre_between_sd, probs = c(0.025, 0.975))
genre_b_share      <- het_share(genre_between_sd)
genre_b_share_mean <- mean(genre_b_share)
genre_b_share_ci   <- quantile(genre_b_share, probs = c(0.025, 0.975))
genre_b_pair       <- pair_share(genre_between_sd)
genre_b_pair_mean  <- mean(genre_b_pair)
genre_b_pair_ci    <- quantile(genre_b_pair, probs = c(0.025, 0.975))

# Centre of M2's genre-effect distribution at each draw: the mean of the 14
# coefficients (compared with M3's estimated centres mu in the Results; define
# once).
genre_mean_within  <- rowMeans(within_mat)
genre_mean_between <- rowMeans(between_mat)
genre_mean_within_ci  <- quantile(genre_mean_within, probs = c(0.025, 0.975))
genre_mean_between_ci <- quantile(genre_mean_between, probs = c(0.025, 0.975))

# Share of the genre-effect distribution, Normal(centre, spread), lying
# OUTSIDE the ROPE at each draw (Vuorre et al.'s p_ROPE, complemented). Unlike
# het_share(), this depends on the centre as well as the spread; it describes
# whether the associations are practically null in every genre, not whether
# genres differ. Description only: no H2 verdict rests on it.
genre_rope_out <- pnorm(-sesoi, genre_mean_within, genre_effect_sd) +
  (1 - pnorm(sesoi, genre_mean_within, genre_effect_sd))
genre_rope_out_mean <- mean(genre_rope_out)
genre_rope_out_ci   <- quantile(genre_rope_out, probs = c(0.025, 0.975))
genre_rope_out_b <- pnorm(-sesoi, genre_mean_between, genre_between_sd) +
  (1 - pnorm(sesoi, genre_mean_between, genre_between_sd))
genre_rope_out_b_mean <- mean(genre_rope_out_b)
genre_rope_out_b_ci   <- quantile(genre_rope_out_b, probs = c(0.025, 0.975))
```

```{r}
#| label: txt-genre-differences-h2-2
#| include: false

# Inline quantities for the paragraph(s) below, defined once here so the
# prose reads `r name` rather than a formatting call.
txt_genre_sd_mean <- round(genre_sd_mean, 3)
txt_genre_sd_ci_lo <- round(genre_sd_ci[1], 3)
txt_genre_sd_ci_hi <- round(genre_sd_ci[2], 3)
txt_genre_share_mean_pct <- round(genre_share_mean * 100, 1)
txt_genre_share_ci_lo_pct <- round(genre_share_ci[1] * 100, 1)
txt_genre_share_ci_hi_pct <- round(genre_share_ci[2] * 100, 1)
txt_genre_share_n_genres <- fmt_n14(genre_share_mean)
txt_genre_pair_mean_pct <- round(genre_pair_mean * 100, 1)
txt_genre_pair_ci_lo_pct <- round(genre_pair_ci[1] * 100, 1)
txt_genre_pair_ci_hi_pct <- round(genre_pair_ci[2] * 100, 1)
txt_genre_bsd_mean <- round(genre_bsd_mean, 3)
txt_genre_bsd_ci_lo <- round(genre_bsd_ci[1], 3)
txt_genre_bsd_ci_hi <- round(genre_bsd_ci[2], 3)
txt_genre_b_share_mean_pct <- round(genre_b_share_mean * 100, 1)
txt_genre_b_share_ci_lo_pct <- round(genre_b_share_ci[1] * 100, 1)
txt_genre_b_share_ci_hi_pct <- round(genre_b_share_ci[2] * 100, 1)
txt_genre_b_share_n_genres <- fmt_n14(genre_b_share_mean)
txt_genre_b_pair_mean_pct <- round(genre_b_pair_mean * 100, 1)
txt_genre_b_pair_ci_lo_pct <- round(genre_b_pair_ci[1] * 100, 1)
txt_genre_b_pair_ci_hi_pct <- round(genre_b_pair_ci[2] * 100, 1)
txt_genre_rope_out_mean_pct <- round(genre_rope_out_mean * 100, 1)
txt_genre_rope_out_ci_lo_pct <- round(genre_rope_out_ci[1] * 100, 1)
txt_genre_rope_out_ci_hi_pct <- round(genre_rope_out_ci[2] * 100, 1)
txt_genre_rope_out_b_mean_pct <- round(genre_rope_out_b_mean * 100, 1)
txt_genre_rope_out_b_ci_lo_pct <- round(genre_rope_out_b_ci[1] * 100, 1)
txt_genre_rope_out_b_ci_hi_pct <- round(genre_rope_out_b_ci[2] * 100, 1)
# Mean of the 14 M2 coefficients (compared with M3's mu in the M3 paragraph);
# sprintf keeps trailing zeros (e.g. -0.010).
txt_m2_mean_within        <- sprintf('%.3f', mean(genre_mean_within))
txt_m2_mean_within_ci_lo  <- sprintf('%.3f', genre_mean_within_ci[1])
txt_m2_mean_within_ci_hi  <- sprintf('%.3f', genre_mean_within_ci[2])
txt_m2_mean_between       <- sprintf('%.3f', mean(genre_mean_between))
txt_m2_mean_between_ci_lo <- sprintf('%.3f', genre_mean_between_ci[1])
txt_m2_mean_between_ci_hi <- sprintf('%.3f', genre_mean_between_ci[2])
```

The joint Wald test shows whether the coefficients differ, but not which ones differ or by how much. To describe the size of the differences from the same model, we computed the SD of the 14 genre coefficients at each posterior draw of the Bayesian fit of M2, and from it the descriptors defined in the Methods; none of them was preregistered, and none was converted into a verdict. Within persons, the SD averaged `r txt_genre_sd_mean` (95% CI: \[`r txt_genre_sd_ci_lo`, `r txt_genre_sd_ci_hi`\]; @fig-h2-heterogeneity, top row). It implied that `r txt_genre_share_mean_pct`% of genres (95% CI \[`r txt_genre_share_ci_lo_pct`%, `r txt_genre_share_ci_hi_pct`%\]) lay more than 0.06 from the average genre effect, an expected `r txt_genre_share_n_genres` of the 14, and that `r txt_genre_pair_mean_pct`% of genre pairs (95% CI \[`r txt_genre_pair_ci_lo_pct`%, `r txt_genre_pair_ci_hi_pct`%\]) differed by more than 0.06. Between persons, the SD averaged `r txt_genre_bsd_mean` (95% CI: \[`r txt_genre_bsd_ci_lo`, `r txt_genre_bsd_ci_hi`\]), which implied that `r txt_genre_b_share_mean_pct`% of genres (95% CI \[`r txt_genre_b_share_ci_lo_pct`%, `r txt_genre_b_share_ci_hi_pct`%\]) lay more than 0.06 from the average genre effect, an expected `r txt_genre_b_share_n_genres` of the 14, and that `r txt_genre_b_pair_mean_pct`% of genre pairs (95% CI \[`r txt_genre_b_pair_ci_lo_pct`%, `r txt_genre_b_pair_ci_hi_pct`%\]) differed by more than 0.06. Because M2 estimates the 14 coefficients independently, each carries its own estimation noise, which is large for rarely played genres, and the SD of the 14 estimates, and the shares derived from it, can therefore overstate how much the genres truly differ.

```{r}
#| label: integrated-coefs-extract
#| include: false
#| eval: true

# --- M2 (independent coefficients): extract within and between ---
m2_within <- broom.mixed::tidy(h2_model, conf.int = TRUE) |>
  filter(grepl("^gh_.*_within$", term), effect == "fixed") |>
  mutate(
    genre = prettify_genre(sub("^gh_(.*)_within$", "\\1", term)),
    model = "M2: Independent coefficients"
  ) |>
  select(model, genre, estimate, std.error, conf.low, conf.high)

m2_between <- broom.mixed::tidy(h2_model, conf.int = TRUE) |>
  filter(grepl("^gh_.*_between$", term), effect == "fixed") |>
  mutate(
    genre = prettify_genre(sub("^gh_(.*)_between$", "\\1", term)),
    model = "M2: Independent coefficients"
  ) |>
  select(model, genre, estimate, std.error, conf.low, conf.high)

# --- M4 (multi-membership): genre slopes = overall slope + genre adjustment ---
# M4's genre adjustments are deviations from the overall total_within /
# total_between fixed effects. To make them comparable to M2/M3's absolute
# genre coefficients, we add the overall slope back draw by draw, so that the
# intervals carry the uncertainty of the overall slope and its posterior
# correlation with each adjustment (h2_mm_draws comes from chunk h2-mm-h1).
m4_re <- ranef(h2_mm_model)
mm_key <- names(m4_re)[grepl("^mm", names(m4_re))][1]

m4_genre_slopes <- function(dim) {
  nm   <- names(h2_mm_draws)
  cols <- nm[startsWith(nm, paste0("r_", mm_key, "[")) &
               endsWith(nm, paste0(",total_", dim, "]"))]
  stopifnot(length(cols) == length(gh_within))
  purrr::map_dfr(cols, function(v) {
    s <- h2_mm_draws[[paste0("b_total_", dim)]] + h2_mm_draws[[v]]
    tibble(
      model     = "M4: Multi-membership",
      genre     = prettify_genre(sub(",.*$", "", sub(paste0("r_", mm_key, "["), "", v,
                                                    fixed = TRUE))),
      estimate  = mean(s), std.error = sd(s),
      conf.low  = unname(quantile(s, 0.025)), conf.high = unname(quantile(s, 0.975))
    )
  })
}
m4_mm_within  <- m4_genre_slopes("within")
m4_mm_between <- m4_genre_slopes("between")

# --- M3 (hierarchical prior): extract within and between ---
# M3 is fitted in non-centred form (chunk h2-hier-fit): each genre coefficient
# is gamma + r_g, computed draw-wise in h2_hier_nc (matrices of draws x 14,
# columns in gh_vars order, i.e. the order of gh_within / gh_between).
m3_genre_summary <- function(beta, dim) {
  stopifnot(ncol(beta) == 14, identical(colnames(beta), hier_genres))
  tibble(
    term      = paste0("gh_", colnames(beta), "_", dim),
    genre     = prettify_genre(colnames(beta)),
    model     = "M3: Hierarchical prior",
    estimate  = unname(colMeans(beta)),
    std.error = unname(apply(beta, 2, sd)),
    conf.low  = unname(apply(beta, 2, quantile, probs = 0.025)),
    conf.high = unname(apply(beta, 2, quantile, probs = 0.975))
  )
}
m3_hier_within_full  <- m3_genre_summary(h2_hier_nc$beta_w, "within")
m3_hier_between_full <- m3_genre_summary(h2_hier_nc$beta_b, "between")
stopifnot(identical(m3_hier_within_full$term, gh_within),
          identical(m3_hier_between_full$term, gh_between))
m3_hier_within  <- m3_hier_within_full |>
  select(model, genre, estimate, std.error, conf.low, conf.high)
m3_hier_between <- m3_hier_between_full |>
  select(model, genre, estimate, std.error, conf.low, conf.high)

# --- Combine ---
# Within-person: all three models (M2 FE, M3 Hier, M4 MM)
all_within  <- bind_rows(m2_within, m3_hier_within, m4_mm_within)
# Between-person: all three models (M4 now has full within + between)
all_between <- bind_rows(m2_between, m3_hier_between, m4_mm_between)

# Guard for the Discussion's per-genre paragraph: all 14 within-person
# point estimates lie within a third of the SESOI (|estimate| < 0.02).
stopifnot(max(abs(m3_hier_within$estimate)) < 0.02)
# Discussion heading 'close to zero in every genre': every M3 between-person
# point estimate lies inside the ROPE (narrow the heading rather than loosen this).
stopifnot(max(abs(m3_hier_between$estimate)) < 0.06)

# Per-model interval verdicts and spreads for the per-genre prose
rope_count <- function(d) sum(d$conf.low > -0.06 & d$conf.high < 0.06)
m2_w_in_rope <- rope_count(m2_within)
m2_b_in_rope <- rope_count(m2_between)
m2_w_widths  <- m2_within$conf.high - m2_within$conf.low
m2_widest_genre <- m2_within$genre[which.max(m2_w_widths)]
m2_width_ratio  <- max(m2_w_widths) / min(m2_w_widths)
# Discussion caveat: the widest M2 within-person interval belongs to one of the
# seven least-played genres (rank14 is ordered by in-study playtime, descending)
norm_lab <- function(x) gsub("[^a-z]", "", tolower(x))
stopifnot(norm_lab(m2_widest_genre) %in% norm_lab(tail(rank14, 7)))
m4_w_in_rope <- rope_count(m4_mm_within)
m4_b_in_rope <- rope_count(m4_mm_between)
m4_w_range <- range(m4_mm_within$estimate)
m4_b_range <- range(m4_mm_between$estimate)
# Guard the fixed prose: no M2 interval sits entirely outside the ROPE
# ("the remainder straddle a boundary rather than exclude it")
stopifnot(
  all(m2_within$conf.high > -0.06 & m2_within$conf.low < 0.06),
  all(m2_between$conf.high > -0.06 & m2_between$conf.low < 0.06)
)

# Order genres by the M3 (hierarchical prior) within-person estimate; the
# shared y-axis requires a single ordering across both facets.
genre_order_within <- m3_hier_within |> arrange(estimate) |> pull(genre)

all_coefs <- bind_rows(
  all_within  |> mutate(dimension = "Within-person (H2a)"),
  all_between |> mutate(dimension = "Between-person (H2b)")
) |>
  mutate(dimension = factor(dimension, levels = c(
    "Within-person (H2a)", "Between-person (H2b)"
  )))
```

```{r}
#| label: txt-genre-differences-h2-3
#| include: false

# Inline quantities for the paragraph(s) below, defined once here so the
# prose reads `r name` rather than a formatting call.
txt_m2_width_ratio <- round(m2_width_ratio)
txt_m4_w_range_lo <- round(m4_w_range[1], 3)
txt_m4_w_range_hi <- round(m4_w_range[2], 3)
txt_m4_b_range_lo <- round(m4_b_range[1], 3)
txt_m4_b_range_hi <- round(m4_b_range[2], 3)
```

@fig-integrated-coefs (blue circles) shows the per-genre estimates from M2. The 14 within-person point estimates clustered near zero, and `r m2_w_in_rope` of the 14 credible intervals fell entirely inside the ROPE; the remainder straddled a boundary rather than excluding it. The cost of independent estimation showed in the interval widths: the widest within-person interval (`r m2_widest_genre`) was about `r txt_m2_width_ratio` times wider than the narrowest, too wide to support a conclusion about any rarely played genre. Between persons the intervals were wider still, with `r m2_b_in_rope` of the 14 entirely inside the ROPE.

### Exploratory Models (M3 and M4)

```{r}
#| label: h2-hier-tau
#| dependson: "h2-joint-test"
#| include: false
#| eval: true

# M3 hyperparameters from the non-centred fit (chunk h2-hier-fit; h2_hier_nc
# holds the draws): tau_within and tau_between are the SDs of the two
# multi-membership genre intercepts (sd_mmgW_...__Intercept and
# sd_mmgB_...__Intercept), and the common genre effects gamma_W and gamma_B
# are the slopes on the summed exposures (b_sum_within, b_sum_between).
h2_hier_vars <- brms::variables(h2_hier_model)
stopifnot(
  c("b_sum_within", "b_sum_between",
    paste0("sd_", h2_hier_nc$group_w, "__Intercept"),
    paste0("sd_", h2_hier_nc$group_b, "__Intercept")) %in% h2_hier_vars,
  sum(startsWith(h2_hier_vars, paste0("r_", h2_hier_nc$group_w, "["))) == 14,
  sum(startsWith(h2_hier_vars, paste0("r_", h2_hier_nc$group_b, "["))) == 14,
  length(h2_hier_nc$tau_w) == nrow(h2_hier_nc$beta_w)
)

# H2a: within-person genre heterogeneity
tau_draws <- h2_hier_nc$tau_w
tau_mean  <- mean(tau_draws)
tau_ci    <- quantile(tau_draws, c(0.025, 0.975))
tau_in_rope <- mean(tau_draws > -0.06 & tau_draws < 0.06)
# Posterior share below the reference value het_thr: descriptive only, set
# against the prior's share in the M3 paragraph (txt_tau_prior_below_pct).
tau_p_thr      <- mean(tau_draws < het_thr)
tau_share      <- het_share(tau_draws)
tau_share_mean <- mean(tau_share)
tau_share_ci   <- quantile(tau_share, c(0.025, 0.975))
tau_pair       <- pair_share(tau_draws)
tau_pair_mean  <- mean(tau_pair)
tau_pair_ci    <- quantile(tau_pair, c(0.025, 0.975))

# H2b: between-person genre heterogeneity
tau_between_draws <- h2_hier_nc$tau_b
tau_between_mean  <- mean(tau_between_draws)
tau_between_ci    <- quantile(tau_between_draws, c(0.025, 0.975))
tau_between_in_rope <- mean(tau_between_draws > -0.06 & tau_between_draws < 0.06)
tau_b_share      <- het_share(tau_between_draws)
tau_b_share_mean <- mean(tau_b_share)
tau_b_share_ci   <- quantile(tau_b_share, c(0.025, 0.975))
tau_b_pair       <- pair_share(tau_between_draws)
tau_b_pair_mean  <- mean(tau_b_pair)
tau_b_pair_ci    <- quantile(tau_b_pair, c(0.025, 0.975))

# Common genre effects: the estimated centres gamma_W / gamma_B of the
# genre-coefficient distributions, i.e. the slopes on the summed exposures in
# the non-centred form (b_sum_within / b_sum_between; the mu_* names are kept
# for the downstream chunks).
mu_w_draws <- h2_hier_nc$gamma_w
mu_w_mean  <- mean(mu_w_draws)
mu_w_ci    <- quantile(mu_w_draws, c(0.025, 0.975))
mu_b_draws <- h2_hier_nc$gamma_b
mu_b_mean  <- mean(mu_b_draws)
mu_b_ci    <- quantile(mu_b_draws, c(0.025, 0.975))
stopifnot(length(mu_w_draws) == length(tau_draws),
          length(mu_b_draws) == length(tau_between_draws))

# Share of the genre-effect distribution, Normal(mu, tau), outside the ROPE
# (see h2-joint-test), evaluated at each draw with M3's estimated centre.
# Unlike tau_share / tau_b_share (spread around the centre), it depends on mu
# as well as tau.
rope_out_mu <- function(m, s) pnorm(-sesoi, m, s) + 1 - pnorm(sesoi, m, s)
tau_rope_out        <- rope_out_mu(mu_w_draws, tau_draws)
tau_rope_out_mean   <- mean(tau_rope_out)
tau_rope_out_ci     <- quantile(tau_rope_out, c(0.025, 0.975))
tau_rope_out_b      <- rope_out_mu(mu_b_draws, tau_between_draws)
tau_rope_out_b_mean <- mean(tau_rope_out_b)
tau_rope_out_b_ci   <- quantile(tau_rope_out_b, c(0.025, 0.975))
# (The verdict guard stopifnot(tau_p_thr > 0.95, tau_b_p_thr < 0.95) was
# removed on 2026-10-13: H2 carries no post-hoc negligible/inconclusive
# verdict; the spreads are described, Methods.)
# Guard for the 'In sum' paragraph: between persons, the upper 95% credible
# bound of M2's per-draw SD (h2-joint-test) is more than twice that of M3's
# tau_between.
stopifnot(genre_bsd_ci[2] > 2 * tau_between_ci[2])
```

```{r}
#| label: h2-mm-sigma
#| dependson: ["h2-joint-test", "h2-hier-tau", "h2-mm-h1"]
#| include: false
#| eval: true

# sigma_s_within: SD of genre random slopes on total_within
sigma_sw_col <- names(h2_mm_draws)[grepl(
  paste0("sd_", mm_group_name, ".*total_within"),
  names(h2_mm_draws)
)]
if (length(sigma_sw_col) == 0) {
  sigma_sw_col <- names(h2_mm_draws)[grepl("sd_mm.*total_within", names(h2_mm_draws))]
}
stopifnot(length(sigma_sw_col) >= 1)
sigma_sw_col <- sigma_sw_col[1]

sigma_sw_draws       <- h2_mm_draws[[sigma_sw_col]]
sigma_sw_mean        <- mean(sigma_sw_draws)
sigma_sw_ci          <- quantile(sigma_sw_draws, probs = c(0.025, 0.975))
sigma_sw_above_sesoi <- mean(sigma_sw_draws > 0.06)
sigma_sw_share       <- het_share(sigma_sw_draws)
sigma_sw_share_mean  <- mean(sigma_sw_share)
sigma_sw_share_ci    <- quantile(sigma_sw_share, c(0.025, 0.975))
sigma_sw_pair        <- pair_share(sigma_sw_draws)
sigma_sw_pair_mean   <- mean(sigma_sw_pair)
sigma_sw_pair_ci     <- quantile(sigma_sw_pair, c(0.025, 0.975))

# sigma_s_between: SD of genre random slopes on total_between (the full mm()
# formula includes both total_within and total_between in the mm() term)
sigma_sb_col <- names(h2_mm_draws)[grepl(
  paste0("sd_", mm_group_name, ".*total_between"),
  names(h2_mm_draws)
)]
if (length(sigma_sb_col) == 0) {
  sigma_sb_col <- names(h2_mm_draws)[grepl("sd_mm.*total_between", names(h2_mm_draws))]
}
stopifnot(length(sigma_sb_col) >= 1)
sigma_sb_col         <- sigma_sb_col[1]

sigma_sb_draws       <- h2_mm_draws[[sigma_sb_col]]
sigma_sb_mean        <- mean(sigma_sb_draws)
sigma_sb_ci          <- quantile(sigma_sb_draws, probs = c(0.025, 0.975))
sigma_sb_above_sesoi <- mean(sigma_sb_draws > 0.06)
sigma_sb_share       <- het_share(sigma_sb_draws)
sigma_sb_share_mean  <- mean(sigma_sb_share)
sigma_sb_share_ci    <- quantile(sigma_sb_share, c(0.025, 0.975))
sigma_sb_pair        <- pair_share(sigma_sb_draws)
sigma_sb_pair_mean   <- mean(sigma_sb_pair)
sigma_sb_pair_ci     <- quantile(sigma_sb_pair, c(0.025, 0.975))
# (The verdict guard stopifnot(sigma_sw_p_thr < 0.95, sigma_sb_p_thr < 0.95)
# was removed on 2026-10-13 with the post-hoc H2 verdict; see h2-hier-tau.)

# Share of the genre-effect distribution outside the ROPE (see h2-joint-test):
# M4's pure-genre slopes are Normal(beta, sigma_s), centred on the overall
# playtime slope. mm_beta1/2_draws (h2-mm-h1) are draw-aligned with
# sigma_sw/sb_draws (both from h2_mm_draws).
sigma_sw_rope_out <- pnorm(-sesoi, mm_beta1_draws, sigma_sw_draws) +
  (1 - pnorm(sesoi, mm_beta1_draws, sigma_sw_draws))
sigma_sw_rope_out_mean <- mean(sigma_sw_rope_out)
sigma_sw_rope_out_ci   <- quantile(sigma_sw_rope_out, probs = c(0.025, 0.975))
sigma_sb_rope_out <- pnorm(-sesoi, mm_beta2_draws, sigma_sb_draws) +
  (1 - pnorm(sesoi, mm_beta2_draws, sigma_sb_draws))
sigma_sb_rope_out_mean <- mean(sigma_sb_rope_out)
sigma_sb_rope_out_ci   <- quantile(sigma_sb_rope_out, probs = c(0.025, 0.975))

# Guards for the fixed prose (2026-10-13, descriptive H2):
# - ROPE-share paragraph: within persons the share is smallest under M3;
# - paragraph after fig-h2-heterogeneity, 'In sum', the abstract and the
#   Discussion: within persons M4's sigma_s is less precise (wider 95% CI)
#   than M3's tau;
# - Discussion: at the upper 95% credible bound of sigma_s_within, at least
#   one of the 14 genres is expected more than 0.06 from the average slope
#   ("differences confined to a few genres cannot be excluded");
# - the title ("practically null and vary little across video game genres") and the Discussion
#   rest on the per-genre ROPE results and on M3's ROPE shares: on average
#   less than 5% of M3's genre-effect distribution lies outside the ROPE, on
#   both dimensions.
stopifnot(
  tau_rope_out_mean < genre_rope_out_mean,
  tau_rope_out_mean < sigma_sw_rope_out_mean,
  diff(sigma_sw_ci) > diff(tau_ci),
  14 * sigma_sw_share_ci[2] >= 1,
  tau_rope_out_mean < 0.05,
  tau_rope_out_b_mean < 0.05
)
```

```{r}
#| label: h2-heterogeneity-extract
#| include: false
#| eval: true

# Reuse draws already extracted in this section:
#   M2: genre_effect_sd / genre_between_sd   (h2-joint-test)
#   M3: tau_draws / tau_between_draws        (h2-hier-tau)
#   M4: sigma_sw_draws / sigma_sb_draws      (h2-mm-sigma)
m2_sd_within_per_draw  <- genre_effect_sd
m2_sd_between_per_draw <- genre_between_sd

h2_het_draws <- bind_rows(
  # Within-person (H2a)
  tibble(dimension = "Within-person (H2a)", model = "M2: Independent coefficients (SD)", value = m2_sd_within_per_draw),
  tibble(dimension = "Within-person (H2a)", model = "M3: Hierarchical prior (τ)", value = tau_draws),
  tibble(dimension = "Within-person (H2a)", model = "M4: Multi-membership (σ_s)", value = sigma_sw_draws),
  # Between-person (H2b)
  tibble(dimension = "Between-person (H2b)", model = "M2: Independent coefficients (SD)", value = m2_sd_between_per_draw),
  tibble(dimension = "Between-person (H2b)", model = "M3: Hierarchical prior (τ)", value = tau_between_draws),
  tibble(dimension = "Between-person (H2b)", model = "M4: Multi-membership (σ_s)", value = sigma_sb_draws)
) |>
  mutate(
    # Reversed so the lowest model (M2) displays at the top
    model = factor(model, levels = c(
      "M4: Multi-membership (σ_s)",
      "M3: Hierarchical prior (τ)",
      "M2: Independent coefficients (SD)"
    )),
    dimension = factor(dimension, levels = c(
      "Within-person (H2a)", "Between-person (H2b)"
    ))
  )
```

```{r}
txt_tau_pair_ci_hi_pct <- round(tau_pair_ci[2] * 100, 1)
txt_tau_between_mean <- round(tau_between_mean, 3)

txt_tau_between_ci_hi <- round(tau_between_ci[2], 3)

txt_tau_b_share_ci_hi_pct <- round(tau_b_share_ci[2] * 100, 1)

txt_tau_b_pair_ci_hi_pct <- round(tau_b_pair_ci[2] * 100, 1)
txt_tau_rope_out_mean_pct <- round(tau_rope_out_mean * 100, 1)

txt_tau_rope_out_ci_hi_pct <- round(tau_rope_out_ci[2] * 100, 1)
txt_tau_rope_out_b_mean_pct <- round(tau_rope_out_b_mean * 100, 1)
txt_tau_rope_out_b_ci_lo_pct <- round(tau_rope_out_b_ci[1] * 100, 1)
txt_tau_rope_out_b_ci_hi_pct <- round(tau_rope_out_b_ci[2] * 100, 1)
# M3's common genre effects, set beside the M2 means (txt_m2_mean_*), which
# use the same sprintf format so that trailing zeros are kept (e.g. -0.010).
txt_mu_w_mean  <- sprintf('%.3f', mu_w_mean)
txt_mu_w_ci_lo <- sprintf('%.3f', mu_w_ci[1])
txt_mu_w_ci_hi <- sprintf('%.3f', mu_w_ci[2])
txt_mu_b_mean  <- sprintf('%.3f', mu_b_mean)
txt_mu_b_ci_lo <- sprintf('%.3f', mu_b_ci[1])
txt_mu_b_ci_hi <- sprintf('%.3f', mu_b_ci[2])
# Prior mass of tau's half-Student-t(3, 0, tau_prior_scale) prior (chunk
# h2-hier-fit; brms default sd form) below the reference value het_thr,
# against the posterior share (txt_tau_p_thr_pct). Until 2026-10-13 this was
# the Half-Normal(0, 0.1) mass, 2 * pnorm(het_thr / 0.1) - 1.
txt_tau_prior_below_pct <- round(100 * 2 * (pt(het_thr / tau_prior_scale, df = 3) - 0.5), 1)
stopifnot(txt_tau_prior_below_pct < 50)
# The Results say the concentration of tau_within at small values comes from
# the data rather than the prior: the posterior share below the reference
# value must dwarf the prior share.
stopifnot(txt_tau_p_thr_pct > 10 * txt_tau_prior_below_pct)
```

```{r}
#| label: h2-hier-genre-coefs
#| include: false
#| eval: true

# Per-genre M3 coefficients, beta_g = gamma + r_g computed draw-wise from the
# non-centred fit (m3_hier_*_full, chunk integrated-coefs-extract), in the
# column layout of summary()$fixed that the code below uses.
m3_as_fixed <- function(d) {
  d |>
    transmute(term, Estimate = estimate, Est.Error = std.error,
              `l-95% CI` = conf.low, `u-95% CI` = conf.high, genre)
}
hier_within_coefs  <- m3_as_fixed(m3_hier_within_full)
hier_between_coefs <- m3_as_fixed(m3_hier_between_full)

n_hier_within_in_rope <- sum(
  hier_within_coefs[["l-95% CI"]] > -0.06 & hier_within_coefs[["u-95% CI"]] < 0.06
)
n_hier_between_in_rope <- sum(
  hier_between_coefs[["l-95% CI"]] > -0.06 & hier_between_coefs[["u-95% CI"]] < 0.06
)
# Guard for the per-genre sentence ("the 14 wider between-person intervals"):
# M3's between-person credible intervals are on average wider than its
# within-person ones.
stopifnot(
  nrow(hier_within_coefs) == 14, nrow(hier_between_coefs) == 14,
  mean(hier_between_coefs[["u-95% CI"]] - hier_between_coefs[["l-95% CI"]]) >
    mean(hier_within_coefs[["u-95% CI"]] - hier_within_coefs[["l-95% CI"]])
)
```

M3 and M4 were specified after the M2 results were known. Under M3, the hierarchical prior model, the spread of the within-person genre effects (H2a) was τ~within~ = `r txt_tau_mean` (95% CI: \[`r txt_tau_ci_lo`, `r txt_tau_ci_hi`\]; @fig-h2-heterogeneity, middle row). This spread implied that `r txt_tau_share_mean_pct`% of genres (95% CI \[`r txt_tau_share_ci_lo_pct`%, `r txt_tau_share_ci_hi_pct`%\]) lay more than 0.06 from the common genre effect, an expected `r txt_tau_share_n_genres` of the 14, and that `r txt_tau_pair_mean_pct`% of genre pairs (95% CI \[`r txt_tau_pair_ci_lo_pct`%, `r txt_tau_pair_ci_hi_pct`%\]) differed by more than 0.06. Between persons (H2b), τ~between~ = `r txt_tau_between_mean` (95% CI: \[`r txt_tau_between_ci_lo`, `r txt_tau_between_ci_hi`\]), which implied that `r txt_tau_b_share_mean_pct`% of genres (95% CI \[`r txt_tau_b_share_ci_lo_pct`%, `r txt_tau_b_share_ci_hi_pct`%\]) lay more than 0.06 from the common genre effect, an expected `r txt_tau_b_share_n_genres` of the 14, and that `r txt_tau_b_pair_mean_pct`% of genre pairs (95% CI \[`r txt_tau_b_pair_ci_lo_pct`%, `r txt_tau_b_pair_ci_hi_pct`%\]) differed by more than 0.06. The prior on τ places `r txt_tau_prior_below_pct`% of its mass below the reference value of 0.031, against `r txt_tau_p_thr_pct`% of the posterior for τ~within~, so the concentration of τ~within~ at small values came from the data rather than the prior. M3 estimated the common genre effects at γ~W~ = `r txt_mu_w_mean` within persons (95% CI: \[`r txt_mu_w_ci_lo`, `r txt_mu_w_ci_hi`\]) and γ~B~ = `r txt_mu_b_mean` between persons (95% CI: \[`r txt_mu_b_ci_lo`, `r txt_mu_b_ci_hi`\]); the means of the 14 independently estimated M2 coefficients were `r txt_m2_mean_within` (95% CI: \[`r txt_m2_mean_within_ci_lo`, `r txt_m2_mean_within_ci_hi`\]) and `r txt_m2_mean_between` (95% CI: \[`r txt_m2_mean_between_ci_lo`, `r txt_m2_mean_between_ci_hi`\]), respectively.

Under M4, the multi-membership model, the spread of the within-person genre adjustments (H2a) was $\sigma_{s,\text{within}}$ = `r txt_sigma_sw_mean` (95% CI: \[`r txt_sigma_sw_ci_lo`, `r txt_sigma_sw_ci_hi`\]; @fig-h2-heterogeneity, bottom row). This spread implied that `r txt_sigma_sw_share_mean_pct`% of genres (95% CI \[`r txt_sigma_sw_share_ci_lo_pct`%, `r txt_sigma_sw_share_ci_hi_pct`%\]) deviated from the overall playtime slope by more than 0.06, an expected `r txt_sigma_sw_share_n_genres` of the 14, and that `r txt_sigma_sw_pair_mean_pct`% of genre pairs (95% CI \[`r txt_sigma_sw_pair_ci_lo_pct`%, `r txt_sigma_sw_pair_ci_hi_pct`%\]) differed by more than 0.06; spreads up to the upper credible bound of `r txt_sigma_sw_ci_hi` points per hour/day remained plausible. Between persons (H2b), $\sigma_{s,\text{between}}$ = `r txt_sigma_sb_mean` (95% CI: \[`r txt_sigma_sb_ci_lo`, `r txt_sigma_sb_ci_hi`\]), which implied that `r txt_sigma_sb_share_mean_pct`% of genres (95% CI \[`r txt_sigma_sb_share_ci_lo_pct`%, `r txt_sigma_sb_share_ci_hi_pct`%\]) deviated from the overall playtime slope by more than 0.06, an expected `r txt_sigma_sb_share_n_genres` of the 14, and that `r txt_sigma_sb_pair_mean_pct`% of genre pairs (95% CI \[`r txt_sigma_sb_pair_ci_lo_pct`%, `r txt_sigma_sb_pair_ci_hi_pct`%\]) differed by more than 0.06.

::: {.place arguments="auto, scope: \"parent\", float: true"}
```{r}
#| label: fig-h2-heterogeneity
#| fig-cap: "*Genre Heterogeneity Under Three Model Specifications (H2).* Left: within-person (H2a); right: between-person (H2b). M2 (top row) is the preregistered model (SD of its 14 independently estimated coefficients, inflated by their estimation noise); M3 (middle row) and M4 (bottom row) are exploratory (τ and σ~s~, model-estimated spreads). Dashed line: reference value of 0.031, the spread at which 95% of genre effects would lie within 0.06 of the average genre effect; the corresponding value for 95% of genre pairs differing by less than 0.06 is 0.022. Both are reference points, not decision criteria (Methods). Thick: 66% credible interval; thin: 95% CI."
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height: 3.2
#| echo: false
#| eval: true

# Reference line only (no shaded band): het_thr is a reference value for the
# spread, not a decision criterion (Methods).
ggplot(h2_het_draws, aes(x = value, y = model)) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = het_thr, linetype = "dashed",
             colour = "forestgreen", alpha = 0.7) +
  stat_halfeye(fill = "grey55", .width = c(0.66, 0.95),
               alpha = 0.7, point_interval = "median_qi") +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = "solid", alpha = 0.4) +
  facet_wrap(~ dimension) +
  labs(x = "Genre heterogeneity (SWEMWBS item-mean per hour/day)", y = NULL) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 13) +
  theme(
    panel.grid.major.y = element_blank(),
    strip.text = element_text(face = "bold")
  )
```
:::

The three estimates in @fig-h2-heterogeneity measure the spread of the genre effects in different ways. M2 estimates each genre independently, so its 14 coefficients are noisy and the SD across them can overstate the spread. M3 and M4 instead pool information across genres: a hierarchical model shrinks the noisier estimates towards the common centre, which reduces the impact of noise and of multiple comparisons [@gelmanWhyWeUsually2012]. Within persons, M4's σ~s~ was less precise than M3's τ, because it describes how the playtime slope changes with the genre composition of a wave rather than how separate genre exposures differ.

M3 shrinks the per-genre estimates towards the common genre effect (@fig-integrated-coefs, orange squares): `r n_hier_within_in_rope` of the 14 within-person credible intervals fell entirely inside the ROPE, as did `r n_hier_between_in_rope` of the 14 wider between-person intervals.

M4 estimates each genre as a deviation from the overall playtime slope (@fig-integrated-coefs, purple diamonds). With the overall fixed effect added back, its within-person estimates spanned `r txt_m4_w_range_lo` to `r txt_m4_w_range_hi` and its between-person estimates `r txt_m4_b_range_lo` to `r txt_m4_b_range_hi`.

::: {.place arguments="auto, scope: \"parent\", float: true"}
```{r}
#| label: fig-integrated-coefs
#| fig-cap: "*Per-Genre Exposure Coefficients Under Three Model Specifications (H2).* Left: within-person (H2a); right: between-person (H2b). Each genre row shows M2 (blue circle; preregistered model, no pooling), M3 (orange square; exploratory, hierarchical prior), and M4 (purple diamond; exploratory, multi-membership). The M2 series is the caterpillar plot specified in the preregistration. Genres ordered by the M3 within-person estimate. Green band: ROPE (±0.06). Thick bars: ±1 posterior SD; thin bars: 95% CI."
#| fig-width: 9
#| fig-height: 6.5
#| echo: false
#| eval: true

# Factor order: M2 top within each genre row, M4 bottom.
# position_dodge with a vertical y-axis places the LAST level at the top,
# so we reverse the desired visual order in the factor levels.
model_levels <- c("M4: Multi-membership", "M3: Hierarchical prior", "M2: Independent coefficients")
model_status_labels <- c(
  "M2: Independent coefficients" = "M2: Independent coefficients (preregistered)",
  "M3: Hierarchical prior" = "M3: Hierarchical prior (exploratory)",
  "M4: Multi-membership" = "M4: Multi-membership (exploratory)"
)

ggplot(all_coefs |>
         mutate(genre = factor(genre, levels = genre_order_within),
                model = factor(model, levels = model_levels)),
       aes(x = estimate, y = genre, shape = model, colour = model)) +
  annotate("rect", xmin = -0.06, xmax = 0.06,
           ymin = -Inf, ymax = Inf, fill = "forestgreen", alpha = 0.10) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = c(-0.06, 0.06), linetype = "dashed",
             colour = "forestgreen", alpha = 0.7) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = "solid", alpha = 0.3) +
  geom_linerange(aes(xmin = conf.low, xmax = conf.high),
                 linewidth = 0.4, alpha = 0.5,
                 position = position_dodge(width = 0.6)) +
  geom_linerange(aes(xmin = estimate - std.error, xmax = estimate + std.error),
                 linewidth = 1,
                 position = position_dodge(width = 0.6)) +
  geom_point(size = 2.5, position = position_dodge(width = 0.6)) +
  scale_shape_manual(values = c("M2: Independent coefficients" = 16,
                                 "M3: Hierarchical prior" = 15,
                                 "M4: Multi-membership" = 18),
                     breaks = c("M2: Independent coefficients", "M3: Hierarchical prior", "M4: Multi-membership"),
                     labels = model_status_labels) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c("M2: Independent coefficients" = unname(model_palette["M2"]),
                                  "M3: Hierarchical prior" = unname(model_palette["M3"]),
                                  "M4: Multi-membership" = unname(model_palette["M4"])),
                      breaks = c("M2: Independent coefficients", "M3: Hierarchical prior", "M4: Multi-membership"),
                      labels = model_status_labels) +
  facet_wrap(~ dimension) +
  labs(x = "Genre coefficient (SWEMWBS item-mean per hour/day)",
       y = NULL, shape = NULL, colour = NULL) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +
  theme(
    panel.grid.major.y = element_blank(),
    legend.position = "bottom",
    strip.text = element_text(face = "bold")
  )
```
:::

The spread describes how far the genre effects lie from one another. Whether the associations are practically null in every genre depends on where the genre effects are centred as well as on their spread, so we also computed, at each posterior draw, the share of each model's genre-effect distribution lying outside the ROPE [@vuorreCommunicatingCausalEffect2024]. Within persons, that share was `r txt_genre_rope_out_mean_pct`% under M2 (95% CI: \[`r txt_genre_rope_out_ci_lo_pct`%, `r txt_genre_rope_out_ci_hi_pct`%\]), `r txt_tau_rope_out_mean_pct`% under M3 (95% CI: \[`r txt_tau_rope_out_ci_lo_pct`%, `r txt_tau_rope_out_ci_hi_pct`%\]), and `r txt_sigma_sw_rope_out_mean_pct`% under M4 (95% CI: \[`r txt_sigma_sw_rope_out_ci_lo_pct`%, `r txt_sigma_sw_rope_out_ci_hi_pct`%\]); between persons, it was `r txt_genre_rope_out_b_mean_pct`% under M2 (95% CI: \[`r txt_genre_rope_out_b_ci_lo_pct`%, `r txt_genre_rope_out_b_ci_hi_pct`%\]), `r txt_tau_rope_out_b_mean_pct`% under M3 (95% CI: \[`r txt_tau_rope_out_b_ci_lo_pct`%, `r txt_tau_rope_out_b_ci_hi_pct`%\]), and `r txt_sigma_sb_rope_out_mean_pct`% under M4 (95% CI: \[`r txt_sigma_sb_rope_out_ci_lo_pct`%, `r txt_sigma_sb_rope_out_ci_hi_pct`%\]). Within persons, the share was smallest under M3; the M2 shares were inflated by the wide intervals of rarely played genres, and the M4 shares reflected uncertainty in both the spread and the overall playtime slope.

In sum, the preregistered tests answered H2: the within-person genre coefficients were not all equal, so H2a was supported (although not under the preregistered primary-genre attribution; Appendix D), and the between-person test did not detect differences, so H2b was not. The spreads described how large the within-person differences were. Under M3, an expected `r txt_tau_share_n_genres` of the 14 genres lay more than 0.06 from the common genre effect and `r txt_tau_pair_mean_pct`% of genre pairs differed by more than 0.06; the corresponding figures were `r txt_genre_share_n_genres` genres and `r txt_genre_pair_mean_pct`% of pairs under M2, whose SD includes estimation noise, and `r txt_sigma_sw_share_n_genres` genres and `r txt_sigma_sw_pair_mean_pct`% of pairs under M4, whose spread was less precisely estimated. As set out in the Methods, we do not convert these quantities into a verdict on the practical size of the genre differences. Between persons, M2's SD was inflated by the noise in the wide between-person intervals: its upper credible bound was more than twice that of M3's τ~between~. Genre terms did not improve out-of-sample prediction (Appendix D), and the wide intervals for rarely played genres ruled out confident inference about any single genre. Appendix E (@tbl-hypothesis-summary) tabulates the joint tests, the spread estimates and their descriptors, and the convergence diagnostics for the three models; full posterior summaries for all four models are in the supplementary materials.

## Daily Timescale (Exploratory)

```{r}
#| label: daily-fits
#| cache: false   # loads brms fits from models/*.rds; caching would serialise GBs
#| include: false
#| eval: true

# ---- Fits ------------------------------------------------------------------
d_m1_ls   <- readRDS(here("models/daily/m1_daily_ls.rds"))
d_m1_full <- readRDS(here("models/daily/m1_daily_ls_full.rds"))
d_m1_ar   <- readRDS(here("models/daily/m1_daily_ls_ar.rds"))
d_m1_wh   <- readRDS(here("models/daily/m1_daily_ls_wh.rds"))
d_m1_xfl  <- readRDS(here("models/daily/m1_daily_ls_xfl.rds"))
d_xfl_dr  <- posterior::as_draws_df(d_m1_xfl)
d_rx_b1    <- mean(d_xfl_dr$b_xfl_within)
d_rx_b1_ci <- quantile(d_xfl_dr$b_xfl_within, c(.025, .975))
# M3-D in the non-centred multi-membership form (R/fit_daily_models.R, since
# 2026-10-14; the centred _v3 fit had d_m3_divs_centred divergences, chunk
# txt-priors).
d_m3_ls   <- readRDS(here("models/daily/m3_daily_ls_v4.rds"))
d_m4_ls   <- readRDS(here("models/daily/m4_daily_mm_ls.rds"))

stopifnot(nobs(d_m1_ls) == sum(!is.na(daily_frame$life_sat)))

d_extract_m1 <- function(fit, sesoi) {
  dr <- posterior::as_draws_df(fit)
  w <- dr$b_total_within
  b <- dr$b_total_between
  s <- dr$sd_pid__total_within
  list(
    b1 = mean(w), b1_ci = quantile(w, c(.025, .975)),
    b1_rope = mean(abs(w) < sesoi),
    b2 = mean(b), b2_ci = quantile(b, c(.025, .975)),
    b2_rope = mean(abs(b) < sesoi),
    sd_slope = mean(s), sd_slope_ci = quantile(s, c(.025, .975)),
    sd_slope_above = mean(s > sesoi),
    rhat = max(brms::rhat(fit), na.rm = TRUE),
    divs = sum(subset(brms::nuts_params(fit), Parameter == "divergent__")$Value)
  )
}
d_extract_m3 <- function(fit, sesoi) {
  # Non-centred M3-D (as M3, chunk h2-hier-fit): tau = SDs of the two
  # multi-membership genre intercepts, gamma = slopes on the summed
  # exposures; hier_nc_draws() checks that both terms have exactly 14 genre
  # levels in the order of hier_genres (the daily genre columns are the same
  # 14 genres). No daily figure or table uses M3-D's per-genre coefficients.
  nc <- hier_nc_draws(fit, hier_genres)
  tw <- nc$tau_w
  tb <- nc$tau_b
  list(
    tau_w_draws = tw, tau_b_draws = tb,
    gamma_w = mean(nc$gamma_w), gamma_w_ci = quantile(nc$gamma_w, c(.025, .975)),
    gamma_b = mean(nc$gamma_b), gamma_b_ci = quantile(nc$gamma_b, c(.025, .975)),
    tau_w = mean(tw), tau_w_ci = quantile(tw, c(.025, .975)),
    tau_w_rope = mean(tw < sesoi),
    tau_b = mean(tb), tau_b_ci = quantile(tb, c(.025, .975)),
    tau_b_rope = mean(tb < sesoi),
    rhat = max(brms::rhat(fit), na.rm = TRUE),
    divs = sum(subset(brms::nuts_params(fit), Parameter == "divergent__")$Value)
  )
}
d_r1  <- d_extract_m1(d_m1_ls, d_primary)
d_r1f <- d_extract_m1(d_m1_full, d_primary)
d_r1a <- d_extract_m1(d_m1_ar, d_primary)
d_r1w <- d_extract_m1(d_m1_wh, d_primary)
d_ar1_draws <- posterior::as_draws_df(d_m1_ar)[["ar[1]"]]
d_ar1 <- mean(d_ar1_draws)
d_r3  <- d_extract_m3(d_m3_ls, d_primary)

# Draw vectors kept for the daily figure
d_dr1 <- posterior::as_draws_df(d_m1_ls)

d_m4_draws <- posterior::as_draws_df(d_m4_ls)
d_sw_col <- names(d_m4_draws)[grepl("sd_mm.*total_within", names(d_m4_draws))]
d_sb_col <- names(d_m4_draws)[grepl("sd_mm.*total_between", names(d_m4_draws))]
stopifnot(length(d_sw_col) == 1, length(d_sb_col) == 1)
d_sigma_sw       <- mean(d_m4_draws[[d_sw_col]])
d_sigma_sw_ci    <- quantile(d_m4_draws[[d_sw_col]], c(.025, .975))
d_sigma_sw_below <- mean(d_m4_draws[[d_sw_col]] < d_primary)
d_sigma_sb       <- mean(d_m4_draws[[d_sb_col]])
d_sigma_sb_ci    <- quantile(d_m4_draws[[d_sb_col]], c(.025, .975))
d_sigma_sb_below <- mean(d_m4_draws[[d_sb_col]] < d_primary)

# M2-D: independent-coefficient genre specification. Its heterogeneity summary
# is the per-draw SD across the 14 genre coefficients, which includes
# estimation error (sampling-noise inflation), as in the preregistered M2.
d_m2_ls    <- readRDS(here("models/daily/m2_daily_ls.rds"))
d_m2_draws <- posterior::as_draws_df(d_m2_ls)
d_m2_wcols <- grep("^b_gh_.*_w$", names(d_m2_draws), value = TRUE)
d_m2_bcols <- grep("^b_gh_.*_b$", names(d_m2_draws), value = TRUE)
stopifnot(length(d_m2_wcols) == 14, length(d_m2_bcols) == 14)
d_m2_sdw_draws <- apply(as.matrix(d_m2_draws[, d_m2_wcols]), 1, sd)
d_m2_sdb_draws <- apply(as.matrix(d_m2_draws[, d_m2_bcols]), 1, sd)
d_m2_sdw       <- mean(d_m2_sdw_draws)
d_m2_sdw_ci    <- quantile(d_m2_sdw_draws, c(.025, .975))
d_m2_sdw_below <- mean(d_m2_sdw_draws < d_primary)
d_m2_sdb       <- mean(d_m2_sdb_draws)
d_m2_sdb_ci    <- quantile(d_m2_sdb_draws, c(.025, .975))
d_m2_sdb_below <- mean(d_m2_sdb_draws < d_primary)

# Daily analogue of the biweekly spread descriptors (Methods, SESOI), with
# d_primary in place of 0.06 and no verdict. Reference values only:
# d_het_thr = d_primary / 1.96 (95% of genre effects within d_primary of the
# average), d_pair_thr = d_primary / (1.96 sqrt(2)) (95% of genre pairs
# within d_primary of each other); the fig-daily-posteriors caption types
# them as 0.51 and 0.36. Shares are posterior means of per-draw quantities.
d_het_thr    <- d_primary / qnorm(0.975)
d_pair_thr   <- d_primary / (qnorm(0.975) * sqrt(2))
stopifnot(round(d_het_thr, 2) == 0.51, round(d_pair_thr, 2) == 0.36)
d_het_share  <- function(s) 2 * (1 - pnorm(d_primary, 0, s))
d_pair_share <- function(s) 2 * (1 - pnorm(d_primary / (sqrt(2) * s)))
d_tau_w_share    <- mean(d_het_share(d_r3$tau_w_draws))
d_tau_b_share    <- mean(d_het_share(d_r3$tau_b_draws))
d_sigma_sw_share <- mean(d_het_share(d_m4_draws[[d_sw_col]]))
d_sigma_sb_share <- mean(d_het_share(d_m4_draws[[d_sb_col]]))
d_m2_sdw_share   <- mean(d_het_share(d_m2_sdw_draws))
d_m2_sdb_share   <- mean(d_het_share(d_m2_sdb_draws))
d_tau_w_pair     <- mean(d_pair_share(d_r3$tau_w_draws))
d_tau_b_pair     <- mean(d_pair_share(d_r3$tau_b_draws))
d_sigma_sw_pair  <- mean(d_pair_share(d_m4_draws[[d_sw_col]]))
d_sigma_sb_pair  <- mean(d_pair_share(d_m4_draws[[d_sb_col]]))
d_m2_sdw_pair    <- mean(d_pair_share(d_m2_sdw_draws))
d_m2_sdb_pair    <- mean(d_pair_share(d_m2_sdb_draws))
d_m2_rhat <- max(brms::rhat(d_m2_ls), na.rm = TRUE)
d_m2_divs <- sum(subset(brms::nuts_params(d_m2_ls),
                        Parameter == "divergent__")$Value)

# M4-D H1 estimates via its total-playtime fixed effects (mirrors the
# biweekly M1-vs-M4 consistency check in @fig-h1-all-models)
d_m4_b1      <- mean(d_m4_draws$b_total_within)
d_m4_b1_ci   <- quantile(d_m4_draws$b_total_within, c(.025, .975))
d_m4_b1_rope <- mean(abs(d_m4_draws$b_total_within) < d_primary)
d_m4_b2      <- mean(d_m4_draws$b_total_between)
d_m4_b2_ci   <- quantile(d_m4_draws$b_total_between, c(.025, .975))
d_m4_b2_rope <- mean(abs(d_m4_draws$b_total_between) < d_primary)
d_m4_rhat <- max(brms::rhat(d_m4_ls), na.rm = TRUE)
d_m4_divs <- sum(subset(brms::nuts_params(d_m4_ls), Parameter == "divergent__")$Value)
```

The daily-level analyses (M1-D to M4-D) were not preregistered, and every estimate in this section is exploratory. Participants in the analysed daily sample contributed a median of `r d_median_days` diary days, with participation declining from `r txt_d_day1_n` responses on day 1 to `r txt_d_day30_n` on day 30; windows closed at the survey completion timestamp (median length `r txt_d_wh_med` hours), so `r txt_pct_d_zero_play`% of person-days recorded no console or PC play.

@fig-daily-posteriors displays the posteriors against the ROPE. At the daily level, the within-person association between same-day playtime and life satisfaction was positive, at β = `r txt_d_r1_b1` points per additional hour in the standalone total-playtime model (M1-D; 95% CI \[`r txt_d_r1_b1_ci_lo`, `r txt_d_r1_b1_ci_hi`\]), with the lower credible bound at zero and `r txt_pct_d_r1_b1_rope`% of the posterior draws inside the ROPE; the multi-membership model's fixed effect was similar (M4-D: β = `r txt_d_m4_b1`, 95% CI \[`r txt_d_m4_b1_ci_lo`, `r txt_d_m4_b1_ci_hi`\]). The interval widened past zero under two of the three robustness refits (Appendix D). Person-to-person variation in this slope was practically negligible: the random-slope SD was `r txt_d_r1_sd_slope` (95% CI \[`r txt_d_r1_sd_slope_ci_lo`, `r txt_d_r1_sd_slope_ci_hi`\]), with `r txt_pct_d_sd_slope_below`% of the posterior below the SESOI. Between persons, with habitual play measured in full-day hours, participants who played more than others reported slightly lower daily life satisfaction: M1-D gave β = `r txt_d_r1_b2` points per habitual daily hour (95% CI \[`r txt_d_r1_b2_ci_lo`, `r txt_d_r1_b2_ci_hi`\]), a negative lean whose posterior sat `r txt_pct_d_r1_b2_rope`% inside the ROPE; M4-D gave β = `r txt_d_m4_b2` (95% CI \[`r txt_d_m4_b2_ci_lo`, `r txt_d_m4_b2_ci_hi`\]); and the all-responses refit, which scores unobserved play as zero, gave β = `r txt_d_r1f_b2` (95% CI \[`r txt_d_r1f_b2_ci_lo`, `r txt_d_r1f_b2_ci_hi`\]) (@tbl-daily-summary).

At the daily level, we described the genre spreads with the same quantities as at the biweekly level, with the daily SESOI of one slider point per hour in place of 0.06, and again without a verdict; the corresponding reference values are `r txt_d_het_thr` slider points (1 ÷ 1.96) for genre effects around their average and `r txt_d_pair_thr` (1 ÷ (1.96 × √2)) for genre pairs. Within persons, the hierarchical prior gave τ~within~ = `r txt_d_r3_tau_w` (95% CI \[`r txt_d_r3_tau_w_ci_lo`, `r txt_d_r3_tau_w_ci_hi`\]), which implied an expected `r txt_d_tau_w_n_genres` of the 14 genres more than one point from the common genre effect and `r txt_pct_d_tau_w_pair`% of genre pairs more than one point apart. The multi-membership model gave σ~s,within~ = `r txt_d_sigma_sw` (95% CI \[`r txt_d_sigma_sw_ci_lo`, `r txt_d_sigma_sw_ci_hi`\]; an expected `r txt_d_sigma_sw_n_genres` genres and `r txt_pct_d_sigma_sw_pair`% of pairs), and the per-draw SD of M2-D's 14 independently estimated coefficients, inflated by estimation error as at the biweekly level, was `r txt_d_m2_sdw` (95% CI \[`r txt_d_m2_sdw_ci_lo`, `r txt_d_m2_sdw_ci_hi`\]; an expected `r txt_d_m2_sdw_n_genres` genres and `r txt_pct_d_m2_sdw_pair`% of pairs). Between persons, τ~between~ = `r txt_d_r3_tau_b` (95% CI \[`r txt_d_r3_tau_b_ci_lo`, `r txt_d_r3_tau_b_ci_hi`\]; an expected `r txt_d_tau_b_n_genres` genres and `r txt_pct_d_tau_b_pair`% of pairs), σ~s,between~ = `r txt_d_sigma_sb` (95% CI \[`r txt_d_sigma_sb_ci_lo`, `r txt_d_sigma_sb_ci_hi`\]; an expected `r txt_d_sigma_sb_n_genres` genres and `r txt_pct_d_sigma_sb_pair`% of pairs), and M2-D's between-person raw SD was `r txt_d_m2_sdb` (95% CI \[`r txt_d_m2_sdb_ci_lo`, `r txt_d_m2_sdb_ci_hi`\]; an expected `r txt_d_m2_sdb_n_genres` genres and `r txt_pct_d_m2_sdb_pair`% of pairs), again inflated by estimation error.

::: {.place arguments="auto, scope: \"parent\", float: true"}
```{r}
#| label: fig-daily-posteriors
#| fig-cap: "*Exploratory Daily-Timescale Posteriors (Life Satisfaction).* Left: total-playtime effects from the standalone H1 model (M1-D) and the multi-membership model's fixed effects (M4-D). Right: genre heterogeneity from all three specifications: M2-D (SD across the 14 independently estimated coefficients, computed at each posterior draw), M3-D (hierarchical-prior τ), and M4-D (multi-membership σ_s). Green band: ROPE (±1 slider point per hour) for the total-playtime effects. Dashed line in the right panel: reference value of 0.51 (1 ÷ 1.96), the spread at which 95% of genre effects would lie within one point of the average genre effect; the value for 95% of genre pairs differing by less than one point is 0.36. Both are reference points, not decision criteria (Methods). Thick: 66% credible interval; thin: 95% CI."
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height: 4.8
#| echo: false
#| eval: true

d_fig_draws <- bind_rows(
  tibble(panel = "Total playtime (H1-daily)",
         param = "M1-D: within-person", value = d_dr1$b_total_within),
  tibble(panel = "Total playtime (H1-daily)",
         param = "M1-D: between-person", value = d_dr1$b_total_between),
  tibble(panel = "Total playtime (H1-daily)",
         param = "M4-D: within-person", value = d_m4_draws$b_total_within),
  tibble(panel = "Total playtime (H1-daily)",
         param = "M4-D: between-person", value = d_m4_draws$b_total_between),
  tibble(panel = "Genre heterogeneity (H2-daily)",
         param = "M2-D: SD of coefs, within", value = d_m2_sdw_draws),
  tibble(panel = "Genre heterogeneity (H2-daily)",
         param = "M2-D: SD of coefs, between", value = d_m2_sdb_draws),
  tibble(panel = "Genre heterogeneity (H2-daily)",
         param = "M3-D: τ within", value = d_r3$tau_w_draws),
  tibble(panel = "Genre heterogeneity (H2-daily)",
         param = "M3-D: τ between", value = d_r3$tau_b_draws),
  tibble(panel = "Genre heterogeneity (H2-daily)",
         param = "M4-D: σ_s within", value = d_m4_draws[[d_sw_col]]),
  tibble(panel = "Genre heterogeneity (H2-daily)",
         param = "M4-D: σ_s between", value = d_m4_draws[[d_sb_col]])
) |>
  mutate(
    panel = factor(panel, levels = c("Total playtime (H1-daily)",
                                     "Genre heterogeneity (H2-daily)")),
    param = factor(param, levels = rev(c(
      "M1-D: within-person", "M1-D: between-person",
      "M4-D: within-person", "M4-D: between-person",
      "M2-D: SD of coefs, within", "M2-D: SD of coefs, between",
      "M3-D: τ within", "M3-D: τ between",
      "M4-D: σ_s within", "M4-D: σ_s between"
    )))
  )

# Per-panel benchmark geometry: a shaded ROPE for the dose panel; for the
# non-negative spreads only a dashed reference line at d_het_thr (a reference
# value, not a criterion), so the band row for panel 2 is not drawn.
d_fig_bands <- tibble(
  panel = factor(levels(d_fig_draws$panel), levels = levels(d_fig_draws$panel)),
  xmin  = c(-d_primary, 0),
  xmax  = c(d_primary, d_het_thr)
)
d_fig_lines <- bind_rows(
  tibble(panel = d_fig_bands$panel[1], x = c(-d_primary, d_primary)),
  tibble(panel = d_fig_bands$panel[2], x = d_het_thr)
)

ggplot(d_fig_draws, aes(x = value, y = param)) +
  geom_rect(data = d_fig_bands[1, ],
            aes(xmin = xmin, xmax = xmax, ymin = -Inf, ymax = Inf),
            inherit.aes = FALSE, fill = "forestgreen", alpha = 0.10) +
  geom_vline(data = d_fig_lines,
             aes(xintercept = x), linetype = "dashed",
             colour = "forestgreen", alpha = 0.7) +
  stat_halfeye(fill = "grey55",
               .width = c(0.66, 0.95), alpha = 0.7,
               point_interval = "median_qi") +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = "solid", alpha = 0.3) +
  facet_wrap(~ panel, scales = "free") +
  labs(x = "Daily life satisfaction (slider points per hour of play)", y = NULL) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +
  theme(
    panel.grid.major.y = element_blank(),
    strip.text = element_text(face = "bold")
  )
```

## Robustness

Two sensitivity analyses tested whether the conclusions depended on analytic choices. Neither changed the H1 conclusion. Adjusting for age, gender, and ethnicity shifted the H1 coefficients by less than 0.01 points and changed no ROPE verdict (Appendix D, @tbl-sensitivity-demo). Refitting on multiply imputed data (m = 100) left neither H1 coefficient practically significant under the preregistered 90% CI grid (equivalence tests are two one-sided tests at α = .05, which correspond to a 90% rather than a 95% interval; @lakensEquivalenceTestsPractical2017a) but, unlike the complete-case analysis, rejected genre-coefficient equality in neither pooled dimension (Appendix D, @tbl-sensitivity-imputation). Appendix D gives full specifications, results, and diagnostics for both analyses, together with the predictive model comparison and the preregistered frequentist analyses (@tbl-frequentist-registered): no H1 coefficient was practically significant under the preregistered grid with mobile play included or on the earlier sample, and the within-person joint test for H2 rejected equality under full but not under primary genre attribution.

# Discussion

When previous work has reported that time spent gaming carries no meaningful association with wellbeing, a common objection is that surely it must depend on the type of game one plays. After all, a relaxing puzzle game and a competitive shooter should not plausibly have the same effect on the person playing them. Video game heterogeneity is the standing explanation for why aggregate playtime nulls should not be taken at face value: playtime is a poorly specified exposure whose associations average over distinct causal contrasts [@ballouHowVideoGames2025; @magnusson2024harmful], and a null total association can in principle be produced by heterogeneous true effects that offset in aggregate [@yarkoniGeneralizabilityCrisis2022]. Genre is the most widely used name for those contrasts [@starostaTangledWaysClassify2024], which makes it the natural first place to look.

