# Appendix F: Model Specifications and Priors {.appendix}

This appendix gives the equations and priors of the four biweekly models; the Methods describe what each model estimates and why we fitted it (Preregistered Models and Exploratory Models). The daily refits M1-D to M4-D use the same specifications with the daily outcome and exposures; `brms` then sets the intercept location and the standard-deviation scales from the life-satisfaction outcome (Methods, Daily Timescale).

## M1 specification: Total Playtime

M1, the preregistered model for H1, regresses SWEMWBS on the within-person and between-person parts of total playtime, with a random intercept and a random within-person playtime slope for each participant.

$$\begin{aligned}
\text{SWEMWBS}_{ij} &\sim \text{Normal}(\mu_{ij}, \sigma) \\
\mu_{ij} &= (\alpha + u_{0j}) + (\beta_W + u_{1j})\, \text{Time}_{\text{within},ij} + \beta_B\, \text{Time}_{\text{between},j} \\
\begin{pmatrix} u_{0j} \\ u_{1j} \end{pmatrix} &\sim \text{Normal}\left(\mathbf{0}, \boldsymbol{\Sigma}_u\right), \quad \boldsymbol{\Sigma}_u = \begin{pmatrix} \sigma_{u0}^2 & \rho_u\, \sigma_{u0}\, \sigma_{u1} \\ \rho_u\, \sigma_{u0}\, \sigma_{u1} & \sigma_{u1}^2 \end{pmatrix} \\
\alpha &\sim \text{Student-}t(3, \tilde{y}, 2.5) \\
\beta_W, \beta_B &\propto 1
\end{aligned}$$

In this and the following equations, $i$ indexes biweekly survey waves, $j$ participants, and, from M2 onwards, $g$ genres. $\text{Time}_{\text{within},ij}$ is participant $j$'s average daily playtime on Nintendo, Xbox, and Steam (hours per day over the 14 days before wave $i$'s scheduled survey) minus that participant's mean across all of their survey waves, and $\text{Time}_{\text{between},j}$ is that mean; the mean also covers the `r n_swemwbs_incomplete` waves with an incomplete SWEMWBS, which do not enter the models. $\alpha$, $\beta_W$, and $\beta_B$ are the population intercept and slopes; $u_{0j}$ and $u_{1j}$ are participant $j$'s deviations from $\alpha$ and $\beta_W$, so that participant $j$'s own intercept is $\alpha + u_{0j}$ and own within-person slope is $\beta_W + u_{1j}$; $\boldsymbol{\Sigma}_u$ is the covariance matrix of these deviations, with standard deviations $\sigma_{u0}$ and $\sigma_{u1}$ and correlation $\rho_u$; $\sigma$ is the residual standard deviation; $\tilde{y}$ is the sample median of SWEMWBS; and $\propto 1$ denotes an improper flat prior.

## M2 specification: Independent Genre Coefficients

M2, the preregistered model for H2, replaces total playtime with the within-person and between-person exposures to each of the 14 genres, estimates their coefficients independently, and has a random intercept only.

$$\begin{aligned}
\text{SWEMWBS}_{ij} &\sim \text{Normal}(\mu_{ij}, \sigma) \\
\mu_{ij} &= (\alpha + u_{0j}) + \sum_{g=1}^{G}\bigl(\beta_{W,g}\, \text{Time}_{\text{within},g,ij} + \beta_{B,g}\, \text{Time}_{\text{between},g,j}\bigr) \\
u_{0j} &\sim \text{Normal}(0, \sigma_{u0}) \\
\alpha &\sim \text{Student-}t(3, \tilde{y}, 2.5) \\
\beta_{W,g}, \beta_{B,g} &\propto 1
\end{aligned}$$

Here $g$ indexes the $G$ = 14 genres. $\text{Time}_{\text{within},g,ij}$ and $\text{Time}_{\text{between},g,j}$ split participant $j$'s exposure to genre $g$, the average daily hours spent on games carrying that genre label (a multi-genre game's full playtime counts towards each of its labels), in the same way as total playtime; $\beta_{W,g}$ and $\beta_{B,g}$ are their coefficients; and $\sigma_{u0}$ is the standard deviation of the participant intercept deviations $u_{0j}$.

## M3 specification: Hierarchical Prior

M3, an exploratory model, keeps M2's predictors and random intercept but draws the within-person and the between-person genre coefficients from two normal distributions whose centres and standard deviations it estimates.

$$\begin{aligned}
\text{SWEMWBS}_{ij} &\sim \text{Normal}(\mu_{ij}, \sigma) \\
\mu_{ij} &= (\alpha + u_{0j}) + \sum_{g=1}^{G}\bigl(\beta_{W,g}\, \text{Time}_{\text{within},g,ij} + \beta_{B,g}\, \text{Time}_{\text{between},g,j}\bigr) \\
u_{0j} &\sim \text{Normal}(0, \sigma_{u0}) \\
\beta_{W,g} &\sim \text{Normal}(\gamma_W, \tau_{\text{within}}) \\
\beta_{B,g} &\sim \text{Normal}(\gamma_B, \tau_{\text{between}}) \\
\gamma_W, \gamma_B &\propto 1 \\
\tau_{\text{within}}, \tau_{\text{between}} &\sim \text{Half-Student-}t(3, 0, 2.5) \\
\alpha &\sim \text{Student-}t(3, \tilde{y}, 2.5)
\end{aligned}$$

The symbols are as in M2. $\gamma_W$ and $\gamma_B$ are the centres and $\tau_{\text{within}}$ and $\tau_{\text{between}}$ the standard deviations of the distributions from which the within-person and between-person genre coefficients are drawn. $\gamma_W$ and $\gamma_B$ receive the same improper flat prior as the slopes in M1 and M2, and $\tau_{\text{within}}$ and $\tau_{\text{between}}$ describe the size of the genre differences in the within-person (H2a) and between-person (H2b) dimensions. Because the centred form of this model, in which the sampler draws each genre coefficient directly from its normal distribution, produced `r h2_hier_divs_centred` divergent transitions, we estimate it in the equivalent non-centred form $\beta_{W,g} = \gamma_W + \tau_{\text{within}}\, z_{W,g}$ and $\beta_{B,g} = \gamma_B + \tau_{\text{between}}\, z_{B,g}$, with $z_{W,g}, z_{B,g} \sim \text{Normal}(0, 1)$. In `brms` this is a model with slopes $\gamma_W$ and $\gamma_B$ on the summed genre exposures plus two genre-level random terms weighted by the genre exposures (the multi-membership construction that M4 also uses); it changes neither the likelihood nor the priors on $\gamma$ and $\tau$.

## M4 specification: Multi-Membership

M4, an exploratory model, keeps M1's total-playtime terms and participant effects and lets the genre composition of each wave adjust the within-person and between-person playtime slopes. Formally, this is a multi-membership structure: every wave belongs to all 14 genres, and only the membership weights vary, each equal to the genre's share of the wave's summed genre exposure.

$$\begin{aligned}
\text{SWEMWBS}_{ij} &\sim \text{Normal}(\mu_{ij}, \sigma) \\
\mu_{ij} &= (\alpha + u_{0j}) + \Bigl(\beta_W + u_{1j} + \sum_{g=1}^{G} w_{g,ij}\, s_{W,g}\Bigr) \text{Time}_{\text{within},ij} \\
&\quad + \Bigl(\beta_B + \sum_{g=1}^{G} w_{g,ij}\, s_{B,g}\Bigr) \text{Time}_{\text{between},j} \\
\begin{pmatrix} u_{0j} \\ u_{1j} \end{pmatrix} &\sim \text{Normal}\left(\mathbf{0}, \boldsymbol{\Sigma}_u\right) \\
\begin{pmatrix} s_{W,g} \\ s_{B,g} \end{pmatrix} &\sim \text{Normal}\left(\mathbf{0}, \boldsymbol{\Sigma}_s\right) \\
\boldsymbol{\Sigma}_s &= \begin{pmatrix} \sigma_{s,W}^2 & \rho_s\, \sigma_{s,W}\, \sigma_{s,B} \\ \rho_s\, \sigma_{s,W}\, \sigma_{s,B} & \sigma_{s,B}^2 \end{pmatrix} \\
\alpha &\sim \text{Student-}t(3, \tilde{y}, 2.5) \\
\beta_W, \beta_B &\propto 1 \\
\sigma_{s,\text{within}}, \sigma_{s,\text{between}} &\sim \text{Half-Student-}t(3, 0, 2.5) \\
\begin{pmatrix} 1 & \rho_s \\ \rho_s & 1 \end{pmatrix} &\sim \text{LKJ}(1)
\end{aligned}$$

The participant terms are as in M1. $w_{g,ij}$ is genre $g$'s exposure hours in participant $j$'s wave $i$ divided by the summed exposure hours of all $G$ genres in that wave, so a wave's weights sum to one; because exposure uses full attribution, a game with two genre labels adds its hours to both. Waves without genre-labelled play, most of them without any recorded play, receive $w_{g,ij} = 1/G$. $s_{W,g}$ and $s_{B,g}$ are genre $g$'s adjustments to the within-person and between-person playtime slopes; because the weights describe each wave's genre mix, the between-person adjustment follows the wave's mix rather than the participant's habitual mix. The two adjustments are drawn jointly, with standard deviations $\sigma_{s,\text{within}}$ and $\sigma_{s,\text{between}}$ (written $\sigma_{s,W}$ and $\sigma_{s,B}$ in the equation) and correlation $\rho_s$; the LKJ(1) prior on their 2 × 2 correlation matrix is uniform over $\rho_s$.

```{r}
#| label: sim-recovery-summary
#| include: false
#| cache: false

# M4 parameter recovery under the final specification (R/sim_mm_recovery.R,
# run 2026-10-14 with SIM_REPS=20, SIM_ITER=8000). The engine purls the
# manuscript's own M4 chunks, so the fitted model is the manuscript's model.
sim_rec  <- read_csv(here("data/processed/sim_recovery/recovery_summary.csv"),
                     show_col_types = FALSE)
sim_diag <- read_csv(here("data/processed/sim_recovery/diagnostics.csv"),
                     show_col_types = FALSE)
sim_n_reps    <- unique(sim_rec$n_reps)
sim_min_cov   <- min(sim_rec$n_covered)
sim_divs      <- sum(sim_diag$n_divergent)
sim_max_rhat  <- max(sim_diag$max_rhat)
sim_row <- function(lab) sim_rec[sim_rec$label == lab, ]
sim_ssw <- sim_row("sigma_s_within"); sim_ssb <- sim_row("sigma_s_between"); sim_rho <- sim_row("rho_s")
stopifnot(length(sim_n_reps) == 1, sim_n_reps == 20, nrow(sim_rec) == 10,
          sim_min_cov >= 19, sim_divs == 0, sim_max_rhat < 1.01,
          # "estimated with upward bias": both genre-level SD means exceed the truth
          sim_ssw$mean > sim_ssw$true, sim_ssb$mean > sim_ssb$true,
          # "weakly identified": the averaged 95% CrI of rho_s spans most of [-1, 1]
          (sim_rho$ci_hi - sim_rho$ci_lo) > 1.5)
txt_sim_n_reps  <- sim_n_reps
txt_sim_min_cov <- sim_min_cov
txt_sim_ssw_true <- sprintf("%.2f", sim_ssw$true); txt_sim_ssw_mean <- sprintf("%.2f", sim_ssw$mean)
txt_sim_ssb_true <- sprintf("%.2f", sim_ssb$true); txt_sim_ssb_mean <- sprintf("%.2f", sim_ssb$mean)
txt_sim_rho_true <- sprintf("%.1f", sim_rho$true)
txt_sim_rho_ci   <- sprintf("[%.2f, %.2f]", sim_rho$ci_lo, sim_rho$ci_hi)
```

Because this use of multi-membership is unconventional, we validated the specification by parameter recovery. The simulation fits the manuscript's own M4 code, read from this document at run time, to `r txt_sim_n_reps` synthetic datasets of 200 participants over six waves with known within-person and between-person genre heterogeneity. The 95% credible intervals covered each of the ten true values in at least `r txt_sim_min_cov` of the `r txt_sim_n_reps` replications, with no divergent transitions. At this sample size, a fraction of the real one, the genre-level standard deviations were estimated with upward bias (posterior means of `r txt_sim_ssw_mean` within and `r txt_sim_ssb_mean` between persons for true values of `r txt_sim_ssw_true`), and the correlation between the within-person and between-person adjustments was weakly identified (true value `r txt_sim_rho_true`, averaged 95% CI `r txt_sim_rho_ci`), so σ~s~ should be read with its interval rather than its point estimate (simulation report in the supplementary materials).

## Priors


All models use the `brms` default priors [@burkner2017brms]. The slopes have improper flat priors, so that the data alone determine their estimates, which are directly comparable with the preregistered maximum-likelihood analysis; the exception is M3, whose genre coefficients receive the hierarchical prior that defines the model. `brms` places the intercept prior on the intercept with all predictors at their sample means, that is, on expected wellbeing at average playtime (for M3, at the mean summed genre exposure), from which `brms` recovers $\alpha$ after sampling; this prior is Student-$t$(3, `r txt_wemwbs_median`, 2.5), centred at the sample median of SWEMWBS. The residual standard deviation $\sigma$ and every other standard deviation, including the participant-level standard deviations and the genre-level spreads τ (M3) and σ~s~ (M4), have half-Student-$t$(3, 0, 2.5) priors; their scale is the larger of 2.5 and the median absolute deviation of the outcome, which for SWEMWBS gives 2.5. Both τ and σ~s~ are standard deviations of `brms` group-level terms (for τ, in the non-centred form of M3 described above), so `brms` assigns this prior to them by default. Each correlation matrix has an LKJ(1) prior, which for a 2 × 2 matrix is uniform over the single correlation. An earlier version used weakly informative Student-$t$ priors on the slopes and intercept, a Half-Normal(0, 0.1) hyperprior on τ and a Normal(0, 0.3) prior on σ~s~; following co-author review, and after those results were known, we adopted the defaults so that no analyst-chosen scale enters the models.
